program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s binding is ambiguous and appears to select the wrong object: the source image shows a small square DVD case near the center and a separate black object to its right, while the edited image shows two white discs. The traces repeatedly call the right-hand disc the DVD and report it white, but do not establish that it is the DVD referenced by the instruction; the central case/disc may instead be the target, and the edit may have introduced or transformed objects. Refine the binding to identify the DVD using its source-image location and appearance, then compare that same object across source and edited images. The criterion should distinguish complete whitening from partial color change and no progress, while allowing unknown if identity or visual evidence is insufficient. Do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as independent confirmation: they share the same apparent target-selection error. This is a semantic grounding issue, not a transport or dependency failure.
